answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a voter’s influence depends on the probability that walks reach independently trusted vertices, not on raw account count. A sybil cluster separated from the honest meadow by a sparse cut has low conductance, limiting the fraction of walks that cross the boundary. With bounded degree and capped per-vertex weight, min-cut and transitivity bounds thus constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even if its internal whisper network is dense.
